messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Estonian, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Estonian line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Ja ta ei liigu mu näo ees, vaidvastu takistas nii mu teed et, et tagasi pöörduda ma olen sageli pööranud.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

singular *tee* would be more accurate) | | **ch’** (che) | Subordinating conjunction “that” | **et** | “that” | OK | | **i’** (io) | 1st‑person singular pronoun “I” | **ma** | “I” | OK | | **fui** | Past‑historic of *essere* “was / had” (auxiliary) | **olen** | “am / have” (present perfect) | OK (tense rendered by Estonian perfect) | | **per** | Preposition “for, in order to” (marks purpose) | – | – | **UNNECESSARY** | | **ritornar** | Infinitive “to return” | **tagasi** | “back” (part of “back‑turn”) | OK | | **più** | Comparative adverb “more” (frequency) | **sageli** | “often” | OK (captures intended frequency) | | **volte** | Noun “times” (frequency quantifier) | **sageli** | “often” | OK (merged with previous) | | **vòlto** | Verb “turned” (past historic) | **pööranud** | “turned” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention
- **MISSING**: *mi* – the dative “to me” is not expressed in the Estonian version. - **UNNECESSARY**: *si*, *al*, *il*, *per* – these grammatical particles have no direct counterpart in Estonian and are naturally omitted. - **GRAMMAR**: *teed* – plural form; the singular *tee* would better match the singular “cammino”.
All other source tokens are correctly rendered in the Estonian translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Estonian script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Estonian text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 34** - Original: Ja ta ei liigu mu näo ees, - Issue: **MISSING** – the dative pronoun “mi” (to me) is not expressed. - Corrected: **Ja ta ei liigu minule mu näo ees,**
- **Line 35** - Original: vaidvastu takistas nii mu teed et, - Issue: **GRAMMAR** – “teed” is plural; the source noun is singular. Also needs a comma before “et”. - Corrected: **vaidvastu takistas nii mu tee, et,**
- **Line 36** - Original: et tagasi pöörduda ma olen sageli pööranud. - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
